comparator.route: Six DSAI electives in the 36-EC free-choice space
comparator.sourceNotes: The live 2026-2027 Leiden Study Guide establishes a complete 180-EC programme: 120 EC of mandatory courses across Years 1 and 2; 24 EC of mandatory Year 3 components, consisting of AI and Ethics (3 EC), Software Engineering (6 EC) and the Bachelor Thesis Project (15 EC); and 36 EC of elective space. The standard discipline-specific route of six DSAI electives is selected rather than a 30-EC minor plus one DSAI elective because it most directly continues the programme's broad academic identity. The six choices remain an explicit restricted-choice aggregate rather than invented individual selections.

components.name: Restricted-choice DSAI electives

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: The closest match prioritises the broad technical computing, mathematics, software and data-science sequence. This route instead makes cognition, language, philosophy, ethics and embodied intelligent systems central, replacing seven specialist computing and mathematics courses with cognitive-science, philosophy, ethics and robotics courses. The alternatives share 17 of 24 courses and differ by 7 courses (52.5 EC), so they exceed the 30-EC / four-course floor for reasons that follow from the distinct organising concept.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest match owns the nine generator-eligible interests defining the technical data-science and AI core. The seven remaining generator-eligible interests form one coherent cognition, human-intelligence, interaction and responsible-AI direction and support a second feasible programme that differs by seven courses. After that inclusion, no unowned generator-eligible direction remains to justify a third programme; support-only curricular topics cannot generate one independently.

blocks.title: Data science, machine learning & intelligent systems

comparator.note: Six 6-EC courses selected from the published third-year DSAI elective list; the aggregate choice space is preserved without inventing individual selections.

notes.text: Both programmes include substantial programming, mathematics, statistics, machine learning and artificial intelligence. Leiden additionally provides a fixed specialist sequence in computer systems, formal computer-science foundations, security, language and computation, software engineering, an independent thesis and 36 EC of advanced DSAI electives. UCR can combine related courses but does not reproduce that full sequence.

Leiden organises Data Science and Artificial Intelligence as a fixed specialist bachelor with a large advanced elective space. At UCR, comparable subjects are distributed across computer science, mathematics, data science, artificial intelligence, cognitive science and philosophy.
